name: microRNA Replacement Therapy (miRNA Mimic Therapy)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Restore the expression of a deficient or tumor-suppressive microRNA to normalize downstream gene regulation.
molecularDefect: Loss or downregulation of endogenous microRNAs leading to dysregulation of multiple target genes.
diseaseMechanism: Synthetic double-stranded miRNA mimics are incorporated into the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC). The guide strand functions like the endogenous miRNA, repressing multiple target mRNAs by translational inhibition and/or mRNA destabilization.
suitableVariantTypes: Diseases caused by loss of regulatory miRNA function; miRNA downregulation; epigenetic silencing of miRNAs.
typicalDiseases: Hepatocellular carcinoma (miR-34 replacement); Mesothelioma; Non-small cell lung cancer; Experimental applications in cardiovascular and fibrotic diseases.
rnaTargetRegion: 3′ untranslated regions (3′UTRs) of multiple endogenous target mRNAs.
transcriptRequirement: Presence of conserved complementary miRNA-binding sites within target mRNAs.
designRules: Mimic endogenous mature miRNA sequence; optimize strand selection; minimize immune stimulation; validate repression of known downstream targets.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Minimal requirement beyond proper duplex formation for RISC loading.
offTargetConsiderations: One miRNA regulates many transcripts; unintended repression of non-disease targets; seed-sequence-dependent off-target effects.
advantages: Restores physiological regulatory networks; one therapeutic can modulate multiple disease-associated pathways.
limitations: Broad target spectrum increases off-target risk; delivery remains challenging; no approved miRNA mimic therapeutics.
clinicalTrialExamples: MRX34 (terminated Phase I due to immune-related adverse events).
